decision: Retain Small and Medium; regenerate Large and Gigantic independently. Style matching is no longer a requirement.

jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset: generic LARGE machine wreck for a top-down virtual tabletop, transparent background. Independent new illustration.

An anonymous heavy robot has been catastrophically destroyed by fire and an internal explosion. Its remains are an ASYMMETRIC COLLAPSE OF A FEW BIG STRUCTURAL ELEMENTS with smaller broken material caught beneath them, not a heap of many similar little spare parts.
Composition: an irregular, jagged, broadly triangular wreck roughly 2.5 metres across, stretched diagonally. One large thick sheet of armor is torn open and folded back on itself; this is the main visual mass, taking about forty percent of the wreck. Beside and partly under it lies a single heavily crushed industrial actuator/power housing, visibly much larger than a hand-sized motor. A snapped load-bearing steel member bows out from underneath to form one projecting spur. Heat has fused these three major masses together in places. A deep dark break and a few transparent gaps separate them. Modest amounts of small shattered metal, scorched wire and molten drips cling to the main pieces, with fine texture concentrated in the crevices. Clear hierarchy of giant, medium and tiny shapes; large quiet plate surfaces alternate with dense torn edges. The physical pieces suggest the former strength and mass of a LARGE machine without preserving the outline or identity of any particular robot.

Grounded painterly battle-map illustration, cooled heat-buckled steel, bubbled black fused metal, ash-grey burned surfaces, restrained rusty brown and dull metal highlights. Everything is cold and inert. True orthographic view from directly above. One centered wreck contained fully within a square image; longest extent about 90% of the canvas, transparent margins on every edge. Irregular outline with projecting fragments and missing chunks, no symmetry or circular perimeter.
Genuine transparent alpha background and gaps. No ground, base, carpet of ash, cast shadow outside the wreck, smoke, flames, sparks, glowing parts, loose debris field, text, borders, people or gore. No intact head, face, humanoid body, complete limbs, wheels, tank tracks, recognizable vehicle or franchise robot. Avoid a circular pancake, radial arrangement, uniform bed of fragments, piles of identical motors, tiled repeated components, neatly sorted salvage and equally sized evenly distributed parts. The dominant shapes must be the torn heavy STRUCTURE, not a repeated collection of small wrecks.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset: reusable GIGANTIC destroyed-machine token for a virtual tabletop. Brand-new independent illustration with no reference image.

A catastrophic industrial robotic wreck, approximately five metres across. It must convey that a truly enormous machine collapsed here, while remaining generic enough for unrelated units. Show a broken, crumpled and partly melted load-bearing structure, not a circle of loose small components.
Build the composition from three dominant, very unequal masses: an enormous armor slab that has buckled like a folded book and torn raggedly through the middle; a heavy dark structural core with crushed ribs and one broad burst casing visible through the break; and a long twisted support casting bent around and fused to the other pieces. Their overlapping arrangement forms a jagged, roughly hooked / lopsided shape with one long projection and a substantial missing bite from the opposite edge. Strong open gaps and a dark collapsed cavity interrupt the wreck. This is a thick structurally ruined mass viewed from above, with broad solid surfaces and brutal fractures. Sparse tiny mechanisms, sheared fasteners and frizzled wire are embedded at the torn interfaces as SCALE CUES, not spread evenly over the entire image. A large folded plate spans metres; little broken mechanical parts remain a small detail. Some edges have flowed into cold black metal lumps and sagging dull-silver drips. One side has much more mass than the other. Powerful hierarchy and a believable violent collapse.

Naturalistic painted post-apocalyptic game art, charcoal soot, burned steel-grey / chalky ash metal, subdued traces of old paint, neutral light, crisp readable silhouette. No requirement to copy any previous illustration. Strict orthographic bird's-eye view directly overhead, no side view or isometric camera. Single centered connected wreck fully inside a square canvas, longest visible extent about 92%, clean alpha margins. Detailed source appropriate for a 1600x1600 final sprite.
True transparent background, including visible gaps. No floor, terrain, circular base, ring, separate ground rubble, contact shadow beyond the wreck, plume, flames, glow, text, logos or living bodies. No recognizable franchise design and no intact machine anatomy or complete vehicle hull. Avoid regular round shapes, flat circular scrap pancakes, repeated small mounds, symmetrical piles, dense all-over sprinkles, cloned coils or motors, neatly sorted parts and similarly sized components. The image should read immediately as the broken remains of ONE VERY LARGE machine whose principal structural pieces were huge.
